title: Entry check: do you need the on-ramp?
note: 15 questions, about 15 minutes, no notes. 12 or more: skip the on-ramp and start at topic 1.1. Under 12: do the on-ramp first. Public: the answers are in the on-ramp README.

questions.question: What is the value of `x` afterwards?
questions.explanation: x becomes 10, then 20. `=` stores the value on the right in the variable on the left.

questions.scenario: `int a = 17; int b = 5; System.out.println(a / b + " " + a % b);`
questions.question: What is printed?
questions.explanation: Whole-number division drops the fraction (17 / 5 = 3) and `%` gives the remainder (2).

questions.scenario: `int total = 0; for (int i = 1; i <= 4; i++) { total += i; }`
questions.question: What is `total` after the loop?
questions.explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10. The loop runs for i = 1, 2, 3 and 4.

questions.question: How many stars are printed?
questions.explanation: i takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4: five rounds.

questions.scenario: `int balance = 300; int amount = 500; if (amount > balance) { System.out.println("Declined"); } else { System.out.println("Approved"); }`
questions.question: What is printed?
questions.explanation: 500 > 300 is true, so only the first block runs.

questions.scenario: `int score = 50; String grade; if (score >= 70) grade = "A"; else if (score >= 60) grade = "B"; else if (score >= 50) grade = "C"; else grade = "F";`
questions.question: What is `grade`?
questions.explanation: Conditions are checked top to bottom; 50 >= 50 is the first one that is true.

questions.question: What is `amounts[2]`, and what is `amounts.length`?
questions.explanation: Array indexes start at 0, so index 2 is the third element, 90. The array holds 4 elements.

questions.scenario: `int[] a = {3, 8, 2, 8, 5}; int best = a[0]; for (int x : a) { if (x > best) best = x; }`
questions.question: What is `best` after the loop?
questions.explanation: The loop keeps the largest value seen so far: 3, then 8; nothing later is bigger.

questions.scenario: `int count = 0; int[] a = {12, 55, 70, 49, 50}; for (int x : a) { if (x >= 50) count++; }`
questions.question: What is `count`?
questions.explanation: 55, 70 and 50 are at least 50. 50 counts because the condition is `>=`.

questions.question: What is `n` when the loop ends?
questions.explanation: 10 → 5 → 2 → 1. When n is 1, `n > 1` is false and the loop stops.

questions.question: What are `code.length()` and `code.charAt(0)`?
questions.explanation: The string has 8 characters, and index 0 is the first character, 'N'.

questions.scenario: Two `String` variables hold text typed by users.
questions.question: How do you check, in Java, whether they hold the same text?
questions.explanation: `.equals` compares the characters. `==` compares whether they are the same object, which can be false for equal text.

questions.scenario: `static int square(int x) { return x * x; }` and `int y = square(3) + square(4);`
questions.question: What is `y`?

questions.scenario: `static void addTen(int x) { x = x + 10; }` and in `main`: `int v = 5; addTen(v); System.out.println(v);`
questions.question: What is printed?
questions.explanation: The method receives a copy of the value. Changing `x` inside it doesn't change `v`; to get a new value out, the method must return it.

questions.scenario: A program stops with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 5 out of bounds for length 5` in a loop written `for (int i = 0; i <= a.length; i++)`.
questions.question: What is the fix?
questions.explanation: Valid indexes run from 0 to length - 1, so the loop must stop before `a.length`.
